pages.label: Webhook: INITIAL_PURCHASE
pages.title: What does the RevenueDot webhook event INITIAL_PURCHASE mean?
pages.description: INITIAL_PURCHASE is sent when a customer first buys a subscription, including a free trial start. Grant access to the entitlements and record the customer.
pages.answer: The RevenueDot webhook event INITIAL_PURCHASE means a customer bought a subscription for the first time, including the start of a free trial.
facts: Sent to
Every enabled webhook whose filters match
Fields that are specific to it
none beyond the common subscription fields
pages.definition: The first purchase of a subscription, including a free trial start.
causes: A subscription chain that RevenueDot has not seen before is recorded, from the SDK, a store notification (when new purchases are tracked), an import or a web checkout.
`period_type` is `TRIAL` for a free trial and `INTRO` for a paid introductory offer; `NORMAL` otherwise.
It is sent once per chain. A lapsed customer who comes back gets `RENEWAL`, not a second `INITIAL_PURCHASE`.
fixes: Grant the entitlements in `entitlement_ids` until `expiration_at_ms`.
Record `original_transaction_id` as the key for the whole subscription.
In a trial, do not count revenue yet: `price` is the money that moved, and is 0 for a free trial.
Deduplicate on `event.id`: deliveries can repeat, because anything but HTTP 200 is retried after 5, 10, 20, 40 and 80 minutes.
pages.mapping: When a store change arrives for a chain RevenueDot has no stored purchase for, the diff in `diffSubscription` returns `INITIAL_PURCHASE` first. A refunded or already cancelled first purchase also gets a `CANCELLATION` right after it, and an outstanding price increase gets its consent event.

pages.label: Webhook: RENEWAL
pages.title: What does the RevenueDot webhook event RENEWAL mean?
pages.description: RENEWAL is sent for a new paid period: a renewal, a trial converting, a lapsed customer resubscribing, or a recovered billing issue. Extend access to the new expiry.
pages.answer: The RevenueDot webhook event RENEWAL means a subscription started a new paid period, whether by renewing, converting from a trial or coming back.
facts: Sent to
Every enabled webhook whose filters match
Fields that are specific to it
`is_trial_conversion`
pages.definition: A new paid period: a renewal, a trial converting (`is_trial_conversion: true`), a lapsed customer resubscribing, or a recovered billing issue.
causes: The store reports a new transaction on a chain RevenueDot already holds, with a later period start.
`is_trial_conversion` is true for the first paid period after a free trial.
A recovered billing issue and a resubscribe after expiry also come out as `RENEWAL`, as in RevenueCat.
fixes: Extend the entitlements to the new `expiration_at_ms`.
Count the revenue from `price`, which is the money that moved on this period.
Use `is_trial_conversion` to measure trial conversion.
Deduplicate on `event.id`: deliveries can repeat, because anything but HTTP 200 is retried after 5, 10, 20, 40 and 80 minutes.
pages.mapping: `diffSubscription` returns `RENEWAL` when the new state has a later period start and a different store transaction ID than the stored one. `isTrialConversion` is set when the stored period was a trial and the new one is not. An upgrade that starts a new period also adds `RENEWAL` after its `PRODUCT_CHANGE`.

pages.label: Webhook: CANCELLATION
pages.title: What does the RevenueDot webhook event CANCELLATION mean?
pages.description: CANCELLATION is sent when auto-renew is turned off or a purchase is refunded. Access continues to the expiry time unless it was a refund. Check cancel_reason.
pages.answer: The RevenueDot webhook event CANCELLATION means a subscription will not renew, or a purchase was refunded.
facts: Sent to
Every enabled webhook whose filters match
Fields that are specific to it
`cancel_reason`
pages.definition: Auto-renew was turned off, or the purchase was refunded. Access continues to `expiration_at_ms` unless it was a refund. A refund has `cancel_reason: CUSTOMER_SUPPORT` and a negative price.
causes: The customer turned auto-renew off (`cancel_reason: UNSUBSCRIBE`), the store gave a reason such as `DEVELOPER_INITIATED` or `PRICE_INCREASE`, or a billing failure counted as a cancellation (`BILLING_ERROR`).
A refund gives `cancel_reason: CUSTOMER_SUPPORT` and a negative `price`.
It is not the end of access. `EXPIRATION` follows when the paid period ends.
fixes: For an unsubscribe, keep access until `expiration_at_ms` and start your win-back flow.
For `CUSTOMER_SUPPORT` with a negative price, revoke access now.
Use `cancel_reason` to separate voluntary from billing-related churn.
Deduplicate on `event.id`: deliveries can repeat, because anything but HTTP 200 is retried after 5, 10, 20, 40 and 80 minutes.
pages.mapping: `diffSubscription` returns `CANCELLATION` when auto-renew goes off (with the reason from the store, or `BILLING_ERROR` when a billing issue is stored, else `UNSUBSCRIBE`) and, with `isRefund`, when a refund time appears (reason `CUSTOMER_SUPPORT`). One-time purchases get the refund form too.

pages.label: Webhook: UNCANCELLATION
pages.title: What does the RevenueDot webhook event UNCANCELLATION mean?
pages.description: UNCANCELLATION is sent when a customer turns auto-renew back on before the subscription expires. Stop the win-back flow; access never stopped.
pages.answer: The RevenueDot webhook event UNCANCELLATION means a customer turned auto-renew back on before their subscription ended.
facts: Sent to
Every enabled webhook whose filters match
pages.definition: Auto-renew was turned back on before the subscription expired.
causes: The customer resubscribed in the store settings after cancelling, while the paid period was still running.
On Google Play this is a restore (`SUBSCRIPTION_RESTARTED`); on the App Store it is `DID_CHANGE_RENEWAL_STATUS` with `AUTO_RENEW_ENABLED`.
Recovering a failed payment is a `RENEWAL`, not this event.
fixes: Stop any win-back message or offer for this customer.
Mark the subscription as renewing again.
Do not change access: it never stopped.
Deduplicate on `event.id`: deliveries can repeat, because anything but HTTP 200 is retried after 5, 10, 20, 40 and 80 minutes.
pages.mapping: `diffSubscription` returns `UNCANCELLATION` when the stored purchase was unsubscribed and the new state is not, unless the change is a renewal that recovered a billing issue.

pages.label: Webhook: NON_RENEWING_PURCHASE
pages.title: What does the RevenueDot webhook event NON_RENEWING_PURCHASE mean?
pages.description: NON_RENEWING_PURCHASE is sent for a one-time purchase: a consumable, non-consumable or lifetime product. Deliver the item once.
pages.answer: The RevenueDot webhook event NON_RENEWING_PURCHASE means a customer made a one-time purchase that does not renew.
facts: Sent to
Every enabled webhook whose filters match
pages.definition: A one-time purchase: consumable, non-consumable or lifetime.
causes: A one-time transaction is recorded for the first time.
Consumables, non-consumables, non-renewing subscriptions and lifetime products all use this type.
A refund of it is a `CANCELLATION` with `cancel_reason: CUSTOMER_SUPPORT`.
fixes: Deliver the item or grant the entitlement. For a consumable, credit it once, keyed on `transaction_id`.
Count the revenue from `price`.
If `expiration_at_ms` is null the entitlement is for life.
Deduplicate on `event.id`: deliveries can repeat, because anything but HTTP 200 is retried after 5, 10, 20, 40 and 80 minutes.
pages.mapping: `diffNonSubscription` returns `NON_RENEWING_PURCHASE` for a transaction it has not stored, and adds a `CANCELLATION` when that first sighting is already refunded.

pages.label: Webhook: SUBSCRIPTION_PAUSED
pages.title: What does the RevenueDot webhook event SUBSCRIPTION_PAUSED mean?
pages.description: SUBSCRIPTION_PAUSED is sent when a Google Play subscription is scheduled to pause. It will not renew at the end of the period. auto_resume_at_ms says when it resumes.
pages.answer: The RevenueDot webhook event SUBSCRIPTION_PAUSED means a Google Play subscription is set to pause and will not renew at the end of the current period.
facts: Sent to
Every enabled webhook whose filters match
Fields that are specific to it
`auto_resume_at_ms`
pages.definition: A Google Play subscription is scheduled to pause. It will not renew at the end of the period.
causes: The customer chose to pause in Google Play. It happens only on Google Play.
`auto_resume_at_ms` holds when the subscription resumes.
The customer still has access until the period ends. `EXPIRATION` with `expiration_reason: SUBSCRIPTION_PAUSED` follows.
fixes: Keep access until `expiration_at_ms`.
Show the resume date from `auto_resume_at_ms`.
Expect a `RENEWAL` when it resumes.
Deduplicate on `event.id`: deliveries can repeat, because anything but HTTP 200 is retried after 5, 10, 20, 40 and 80 minutes.
pages.mapping: `diffSubscription` returns `SUBSCRIPTION_PAUSED` when an auto-resume date appears on the stored purchase. For Google Play it is set from the pause schedule notification, while the subscription is still active, and again from the paused state.

pages.label: Webhook: EXPIRATION
pages.title: What does the RevenueDot webhook event EXPIRATION mean?
pages.description: EXPIRATION is sent when access ended: the period ran out, billing retry gave up, or the subscription paused. Remove access and read expiration_reason.
pages.answer: The RevenueDot webhook event EXPIRATION means a customer's access has ended.
facts: Sent to
Every enabled webhook whose filters match
Fields that are specific to it
`expiration_reason`
pages.definition: Access ended: the period ran out, billing retry gave up or the subscription paused.
causes: The paid period, and any grace period, passed with no renewal.
`expiration_reason` says why: `UNSUBSCRIBE`, `BILLING_ERROR`, `DEVELOPER_INITIATED`, `PRICE_INCREASE`, `CUSTOMER_SUPPORT`, `UNKNOWN` or `SUBSCRIPTION_PAUSED`.
It is recorded once per period by a scheduled job that runs every minute, so it can arrive up to a minute after the expiry time.
fixes: Remove the entitlements of the subscription.
Use `expiration_reason` to choose the win-back message: a billing error needs a payment prompt.
Keep the customer's data.
Deduplicate on `event.id`: deliveries can repeat, because anything but HTTP 200 is retried after 5, 10, 20, 40 and 80 minutes.

snippet.expect: ask for a new payment method

pages.mapping: A scheduled job (`services/tick.ts`) records `EXPIRATION` for every subscription whose access, grace period included, has ended, and claims each one once so replicas do not send it twice. The reason comes from the stored state: paused, then a billing issue, then the stored cancel reason, else `UNSUBSCRIBE`.

pages.label: Webhook: BILLING_ISSUE
pages.title: What does the RevenueDot webhook event BILLING_ISSUE mean?
pages.description: BILLING_ISSUE is sent when a renewal charge fails. The store retries and access may continue in a grace period. Prompt the customer to fix their payment method.
pages.answer: The RevenueDot webhook event BILLING_ISSUE means a subscription's renewal payment failed and the store is retrying it.
facts: Sent to
Every enabled webhook whose filters match
Fields that are specific to it
`grace_period_expiration_at_ms`
pages.definition: A renewal charge failed. The store retries; access may continue in a grace period.
causes: The store could not charge the customer's payment method at renewal.
`grace_period_expiration_at_ms` is always present and is null when there is no grace period.
RevenueDot also sends a `CANCELLATION` with `cancel_reason: BILLING_ERROR`, as RevenueCat does.
fixes: Keep access until `grace_period_expiration_at_ms` when it is set, otherwise follow the store's guidance for your app.
Ask the customer to update their payment method.
Expect `RENEWAL` if billing recovers, or `EXPIRATION` with `BILLING_ERROR` if the store gives up.
Deduplicate on `event.id`: deliveries can repeat, because anything but HTTP 200 is retried after 5, 10, 20, 40 and 80 minutes.
pages.mapping: `diffSubscription` returns `BILLING_ISSUE` when a billing issue time appears on the stored purchase. Apple's `DID_FAIL_TO_RENEW` and Google's `SUBSCRIPTION_IN_GRACE_PERIOD` and `SUBSCRIPTION_ON_HOLD` all set it.

pages.label: Webhook: PRODUCT_CHANGE
pages.title: What does the RevenueDot webhook event PRODUCT_CHANGE mean?
pages.description: PRODUCT_CHANGE is sent when a customer changes product: an upgrade now, or a downgrade or crossgrade scheduled for the next renewal. product_id is the old product.
pages.answer: The RevenueDot webhook event PRODUCT_CHANGE means a customer switched a subscription to another product, now or at the next renewal.
facts: Sent to
Every enabled webhook whose filters match
Fields that are specific to it
`new_product_id`
pages.definition: The customer changed product: an upgrade now, or a downgrade or crossgrade scheduled for the next renewal. `product_id` is the old product.
causes: An upgrade takes effect at once. The event names the old product in `product_id` and the new one in `new_product_id`.
A downgrade or crossgrade is announced when it is scheduled, and takes effect at the next renewal.
A scheduled switch reaching its renewal is only a `RENEWAL`, because it was announced before.
fixes: For an upgrade, switch the entitlement to `new_product_id` now.
For a scheduled change, keep the current product and plan the switch for the renewal.
Do not treat the old product's end as a cancellation: no `CANCELLATION` or `EXPIRATION` is sent for it.
Deduplicate on `event.id`: deliveries can repeat, because anything but HTTP 200 is retried after 5, 10, 20, 40 and 80 minutes.
pages.mapping: `diffSubscription` returns `PRODUCT_CHANGE` when the product on the chain changes without having been announced (`fromProduct` becomes `product_id`), and when a different `autoRenewProductId` appears for the next renewal.

pages.label: Webhook: SUBSCRIPTION_EXTENDED
pages.title: What does the RevenueDot webhook event SUBSCRIPTION_EXTENDED mean?
pages.description: SUBSCRIPTION_EXTENDED is sent when a period got longer without a new payment: an App Store renewal extension or a Google Play deferral. Extend access to the new date.
pages.answer: The RevenueDot webhook event SUBSCRIPTION_EXTENDED means a subscription's current period was made longer without a payment.
facts: Sent to
Every enabled webhook whose filters match
pages.definition: The current period got longer without a new payment: an App Store renewal extension or a Google Play deferral.
causes: On the App Store, your server extended the renewal date (`RENEWAL_EXTENDED`).
On Google Play, your server deferred billing (`SUBSCRIPTION_DEFERRED`).
The period start does not change, only `expiration_at_ms` moves later. `price` is 0.
fixes: Extend access to the new `expiration_at_ms`.
Do not count revenue: no money moved.
Record why the extension was given.
Deduplicate on `event.id`: deliveries can repeat, because anything but HTTP 200 is retried after 5, 10, 20, 40 and 80 minutes.
pages.mapping: `diffSubscription` returns `SUBSCRIPTION_EXTENDED` when the end date moves later while the period start is unchanged. A refund taken back is excluded, because that is `REFUND_REVERSED`.

pages.label: Webhook: REFUND_REVERSED
pages.title: What does the RevenueDot webhook event REFUND_REVERSED mean?
pages.description: REFUND_REVERSED is sent when a refund was reversed and access is back. Reinstate what the refund removed. renewal_number counts the renewals so far.
pages.answer: The RevenueDot webhook event REFUND_REVERSED means the store took back a refund, so the customer has the purchase again.
facts: Sent to
Every enabled webhook whose filters match
Fields that are specific to it
`renewal_number`
pages.definition: A refund was reversed and access is back.
causes: The store reversed a refund, for example after a customer dispute (Apple's `REFUND_REVERSED`).
The purchase had a `CANCELLATION` with `cancel_reason: CUSTOMER_SUPPORT` before.
`renewal_number` gives the number of renewals the subscription had gone through.
fixes: Restore the access or item that the refund removed.
Undo the refund in your revenue records: `price` is the money that moved back.
Match it to the earlier refund by `transaction_id`.
Deduplicate on `event.id`: deliveries can repeat, because anything but HTTP 200 is retried after 5, 10, 20, 40 and 80 minutes.
pages.mapping: `diffSubscription` and `diffNonSubscription` return `REFUND_REVERSED` when a stored refund time is cleared and the change is not a new period. `recordEvent` adds `renewal_number`, a count of the customer's renewal transactions for that product.

pages.label: Webhook: TRANSFER
pages.title: What does the RevenueDot webhook event TRANSFER mean?
pages.description: TRANSFER is sent when a purchase moved to another customer because that customer restored it. transferred_from and transferred_to list the app user ids. Move the entitlement.
pages.answer: The RevenueDot webhook event TRANSFER means a purchase moved from one customer to another because the second customer restored it.
facts: Sent to
Every enabled webhook whose filters match
Fields that are specific to it
`transferred_from`, `transferred_to`
pages.definition: A purchase moved to another customer because that customer restored it (transfer behaviour `transfer` or `transfer_if_no_active`).
causes: A customer restored purchases on a new app user id, and the project's transfer behaviour moves the purchase to that id.
`transferred_from` and `transferred_to` list the app user ids of both customers.
Besides these, the event has only `store` and `environment` and the subscriber attributes.
fixes: Move the entitlement in your own database from the `transferred_from` ids to the `transferred_to` ids.
Do not treat it as a purchase: no money moves.
Check the project's transfer behaviour if transfers surprise you.
Deduplicate on `event.id`: deliveries can repeat, because anything but HTTP 200 is retried after 5, 10, 20, 40 and 80 minutes.
pages.mapping: When a purchase's owner changes, `recordTransfer` in `services/purchases.ts` records `TRANSFER` with the app user ids of both customers. A transfer made through the customer-extras API records it too.

pages.title: What does the RevenueDot webhook event TEST mean?
pages.description: TEST is sent by the dashboard's Send test event or the webhook test API. It is shaped like a purchase, for no real customer. Use it to check your endpoint and signature check.
pages.answer: The RevenueDot webhook event TEST is a sample event that RevenueDot sends only when you ask for a test delivery.
facts: Sent to
Every enabled webhook whose filters match
pages.definition: Sent by the dashboard's "Send test event" or `POST .../integrations/webhooks/{id}/test`. Shaped like a purchase, for no real customer, so it never carries `experiments`.
causes: You pressed Send test event in the dashboard, or called the test endpoint of the webhook.
It is shaped like a purchase so that your parser meets every field.
It is for no real customer.
fixes: Answer HTTP 200 and do not grant anything.
Use it to check your signature verification against the real header.
Look in the dashboard's delivery log if it does not arrive.
Deduplicate on `event.id`: deliveries can repeat, because anything but HTTP 200 is retried after 5, 10, 20, 40 and 80 minutes.

pages.label: Webhook: VIRTUAL_CURRENCY_TRANSACTION
pages.title: What does the RevenueDot webhook event VIRTUAL_CURRENCY_TRANSACTION mean?
pages.description: VIRTUAL_CURRENCY_TRANSACTION is sent when an in-app currency was credited because a purchase was recorded or a rewarded ad was verified. Credit it in your game once.
pages.answer: The RevenueDot webhook event VIRTUAL_CURRENCY_TRANSACTION means a customer was credited with an in-app currency.
facts: Sent to
Every enabled webhook whose filters match
Fields that are specific to it
`source`
pages.definition: An in-app currency was credited because a purchase of a granting product was recorded (`source: in_app_purchase`), or because a rewarded ad was verified and a reward rule granted currency (`source: ad_reward`, a RevenueDot extension). Not sent for adjustments made through the API.
causes: A purchase of a product that grants currency was recorded (`source: in_app_purchase`).
A rewarded ad was verified and a reward rule granted currency (`source: ad_reward`). For that source, `product_id` and `store` are null.
Adjustments you make through the API do not send it.
fixes: Credit the currency once, keyed on `event.id` or the transaction ID.
Branch on `source` if you treat ad rewards differently from purchases.
Do not treat it as revenue: the purchase has its own event.
Deduplicate on `event.id`: deliveries can repeat, because anything but HTTP 200 is retried after 5, 10, 20, 40 and 80 minutes.
pages.mapping: `recordRawEvent` records it from `services/virtual-currencies.ts` when a granting purchase is applied, and from the ad reward service when a reward callback is verified. It uses its own field set: the common fields plus the currency fields.

pages.label: Webhook: EXPERIMENT_ENROLLMENT
pages.title: What does the RevenueDot webhook event EXPERIMENT_ENROLLMENT mean?
pages.description: EXPERIMENT_ENROLLMENT is sent once per customer and experiment when a customer joins an offering experiment. It carries no app, so app-scoped webhooks do not get it.
pages.answer: The RevenueDot webhook event EXPERIMENT_ENROLLMENT means a customer joined an offering experiment.
facts: Sent to
Every enabled webhook whose filters match
Fields that are specific to it
`experiment_id`, `experiment_variant`, `offering_id`, `experiment_enrolled_at_ms`
pages.definition: A customer joined an offering experiment: the first offerings request that enrolled them. Sent once per customer and experiment, as a production event with no app.
causes: The first offerings request of a customer that matches an experiment's targeting enrolls them in a variant.
It is sent once per customer and experiment.
It is a production event with no app, so a webhook set to sandbox only, or to one app, does not get it.
fixes: Store the `experiment_id` and `experiment_variant` (`a` is the control) against the customer so your analytics can split results.
Do not use it to grant anything.
Use a webhook set to production and all apps if you need it.
Deduplicate on `event.id`: deliveries can repeat, because anything but HTTP 200 is retried after 5, 10, 20, 40 and 80 minutes.
pages.mapping: `services/targeting.ts` records it with `recordRawEvent` in the experiment shape (no `app_id`, no subscriber attributes) the first time a customer is enrolled.

pages.label: Webhook: PURCHASE_REDEEMED
pages.title: What does the RevenueDot webhook event PURCHASE_REDEEMED mean?
pages.description: PURCHASE_REDEEMED is sent when a web purchase is redeemed in the app through a redemption link. The anonymous web customer is merged into the app user.
pages.answer: The RevenueDot webhook event PURCHASE_REDEEMED means a web purchase was redeemed in the app, so the customer who paid on the web is now the app user.
facts: Sent to
Every enabled webhook whose filters match
Fields that are specific to it
`redeemed_from`, `redeemed_by`, `redemption_outcome`, `redemption_platform`
pages.definition: A web purchase was redeemed in the app through a redemption link (`POST /v1/subscribers/redeem_purchase`): the anonymous customer who paid on the web was merged into the app user.
causes: The app called the redeem endpoint with a token from a redemption link after a web checkout.
The anonymous customer who paid is merged into the app user.
`redeemed_from` is the anonymous web buyer and `redeemed_by` the app user id that redeemed it. RevenueDot adds `app_user_id` to RevenueCat's sample.
fixes: Link the web purchase to the app user in your own records.
Grant the entitlements the web purchase unlocks.
Do not treat it as a new purchase: the purchase has its own events.
Deduplicate on `event.id`: deliveries can repeat, because anything but HTTP 200 is retried after 5, 10, 20, 40 and 80 minutes.

snippet.expect: link the web purchase to user_1

pages.mapping: `services/web/checkout.ts` records it when the redeem endpoint moves the web customer's purchase to the app user, using the fields of RevenueCat's sample plus `app_user_id`.

pages.label: Webhook: SUBSCRIBER_ALIAS
pages.title: What does the RevenueDot webhook event SUBSCRIBER_ALIAS mean?
pages.description: SUBSCRIBER_ALIAS is sent when a new app user id joins an existing customer. RevenueCat deprecated it, so RevenueDot sends it only to webhooks that ask for it.
pages.answer: The RevenueDot webhook event SUBSCRIBER_ALIAS means a new app user id was linked to an existing customer.
facts: Sent to
Only webhooks whose `event_types` filter names `subscriber_alias`
Fields that are specific to it
`original_app_user_id`
pages.definition: A new app user id joined an existing customer: `logIn` onto an anonymous customer, `logIn` that merged an anonymous customer into an existing one, Android's alias call, or a restore that merged two customers.
causes: The app called `logIn` and the anonymous customer got a real app user id, or two customers were merged.
RevenueCat deprecated the event and sends it only to older projects.
RevenueDot delivers it only to webhooks whose `event_types` filter names `subscriber_alias`, and always keeps it in the customer's event history.
fixes: Add the new id to the customer's list of ids in your own records.
Subscribe to it only if you need to follow id changes.
Prefer reading `aliases` on any event, which lists every id of the customer.
Deduplicate on `event.id`: deliveries can repeat, because anything but HTTP 200 is retried after 5, 10, 20, 40 and 80 minutes.
pages.mapping: `recordSubscriberAlias` records it when a customer gets a new alias or two customers merge. `OPT_IN_EVENT_TYPES` in `packages/core` keeps it from any webhook that does not name it in its filter.

pages.label: Webhook: PRICE_INCREASE_CONSENT_REQUIRED
pages.title: What does the RevenueDot webhook event PRICE_INCREASE_CONSENT_REQUIRED mean?
pages.description: PRICE_INCREASE_CONSENT_REQUIRED is sent when the store asks a customer to accept a subscription price increase. Remind them to accept before the renewal.
pages.answer: The RevenueDot webhook event PRICE_INCREASE_CONSENT_REQUIRED means a store asked a customer to accept a higher subscription price.
facts: Sent to
Every enabled webhook whose filters match
Fields that are specific to it
identity, `product_id`, `transaction_id`, `original_transaction_id`, `store`, `environment`, `currency`, `country_code`
pages.definition: The store asks the customer to accept a price increase.
causes: On the App Store, the price increase needs consent and the customer has not answered (`PRICE_INCREASE` with subtype `PENDING`).
On Google Play, an opt-in price increase is outstanding, or a price step-up awaits consent.
If the customer never accepts, the subscription ends.
fixes: Show a message in your app that the new price needs their consent.
Watch for `PRICE_INCREASE_CONSENT_APPROVED` or an `EXPIRATION`.
Use `currency` and `country_code` to say which price applies.
Deduplicate on `event.id`: deliveries can repeat, because anything but HTTP 200 is retried after 5, 10, 20, 40 and 80 minutes.
pages.mapping: `priceIncreaseEvents` returns it when the stored consent state changes to pending. Apple's renewal info (`priceIncreaseStatus` 0) and Google's price change details set that state.

pages.label: Webhook: PRICE_INCREASE_CONSENT_APPROVED
pages.title: What does the RevenueDot webhook event PRICE_INCREASE_CONSENT_APPROVED mean?
pages.description: PRICE_INCREASE_CONSENT_APPROVED is sent when a customer accepted a subscription price increase. Record the new price. Access and renewal continue.
pages.answer: The RevenueDot webhook event PRICE_INCREASE_CONSENT_APPROVED means a customer accepted a higher subscription price.
facts: Sent to
Every enabled webhook whose filters match
Fields that are specific to it
identity, `product_id`, `transaction_id`, `original_transaction_id`, `store`, `environment`, `currency`, `country_code`
pages.definition: The customer accepted the price increase.
causes: The customer consented to the increase in the store's sheet.
On the App Store it can also mean an increase that needed no consent was notified.
The subscription renews at the new price.
fixes: Record the new price for revenue reports and stop the reminder.
Do not change access.
Compare accepted and expired customers to learn the effect of the increase.
Deduplicate on `event.id`: deliveries can repeat, because anything but HTTP 200 is retried after 5, 10, 20, 40 and 80 minutes.
pages.mapping: `priceIncreaseEvents` returns it when the stored consent state changes to accepted. Apple's `PRICE_INCREASE` with subtype `ACCEPTED` and Google's confirmed state set it.

pages.label: Webhook: TEMPORARY_ENTITLEMENT_GRANT
pages.title: What does the RevenueDot webhook event TEMPORARY_ENTITLEMENT_GRANT mean?
pages.description: TEMPORARY_ENTITLEMENT_GRANT is accepted in a webhook filter but RevenueDot never sends it, because it never grants access it has not verified with the store.
pages.answer: The RevenueDot webhook event TEMPORARY_ENTITLEMENT_GRANT is never sent, because RevenueDot never grants access that the store has not verified.
facts: Sent to
No webhook: it is never sent
Fields that are specific to it
none
pages.definition: A RevenueCat event type for access granted without a verified purchase, during a store outage. RevenueDot accepts it in a webhook's `event_types` filter and never sends it.
causes: RevenueCat sends it when it grants a temporary entitlement while a store is down.
RevenueDot never has that fact: it does not grant access it has not verified with the store.
During a store outage the SDK keeps the purchase and grants access on the device from the offline entitlement mapping.
fixes: Do not wait for this event. Your handler may keep a case for it so a RevenueCat handler still compiles.
If you migrate from RevenueCat, remove any logic that depends on it, or keep it as a no-op.
Use the offline entitlements guide for how access works during an outage.
Deduplicate on `event.id`: deliveries can repeat, because anything but HTTP 200 is retried after 5, 10, 20, 40 and 80 minutes.
pages.mapping: The type is in `EVENT_TYPES` so a filter that names it is valid, and in `NEVER_SENT_EVENT_TYPES` so nothing produces it. That makes 19 of RevenueCat's 21 event types sent.

pages.label: Webhook: INVOICE_ISSUANCE
pages.title: What does the RevenueDot webhook event INVOICE_ISSUANCE mean?
pages.description: INVOICE_ISSUANCE is accepted in a webhook filter but RevenueDot never sends it, because only RevenueCat Billing issues invoices.
pages.answer: The RevenueDot webhook event INVOICE_ISSUANCE is never sent, because RevenueDot does not issue invoices.
facts: Sent to
No webhook: it is never sent
Fields that are specific to it
none
pages.definition: A RevenueCat event type for an invoice issued by RevenueCat Billing. RevenueDot accepts it in a webhook's `event_types` filter and never sends it.
causes: RevenueCat sends it when RevenueCat Billing issues an invoice.
RevenueDot has no invoicing product, so nothing produces the event.
A web checkout on Stripe sends Stripe's own invoice emails and events, not this one.
fixes: Do not wait for this event.
If you migrate from RevenueCat and used it, take invoices from Stripe's own webhooks instead.
Keep a no-op case for it if you share a handler between both systems.
Deduplicate on `event.id`: deliveries can repeat, because anything but HTTP 200 is retried after 5, 10, 20, 40 and 80 minutes.
pages.mapping: The type is in `EVENT_TYPES` so a filter that names it is valid, and in `NEVER_SENT_EVENT_TYPES` so nothing produces it.
